_readme: Hand-editable master list of every accountability report/alert type Otterling can send.
Set "enabled": false on any entry to fully suppress that report -- for server/mac-origin
types this stops the event from ever being logged or pushed (checked in lockprofile_service.py's
_append_alert); for android-origin types the phone fetches this same file (GET /report-config)
and checks it in AlertReporter.report() before doing anything (no SMS, no local log entry).
A type NOT listed here defaults to enabled=true (fail toward reporting, not toward silence) --
so a newly-added report type in the code still reaches you even if this file is stale.
"source": mac = reported by the macOS daemon; server = reported by the filter-server itself
(Fleet webhook / dead-man's switch); android = reported directly from the phone, never touches
"suspicion": high | medium | low -- how alarming this report is, shown as a short tag on the
SMS sent to the accountability partner (e.g. "[HIGH SUSPICION]"); AlertReporter.kt's
formatBody reads this the same way it reads customMessage. A type not listed here, or missing
the key, defaults to "medium". The welcome SMS (sent once, the first time a partner number is
added -- see AccountabilityPartnerSection.kt) explains what each level means so this tag alone
is enough context on every later message.
No restart needed after editing -- lockprofile_service.py re-reads this file on every event,
and the phone re-fetches it once per MacTamperPollWorker cycle (roughly every 15 minutes).

lock_profile_removed.description: The macOS configuration profile (DNS floor) was removed.

vpn_active.description: A VPN came up on the Mac, routing traffic around the content filter.

vpn_cleared.description: The Mac's VPN went back down; filter is back in effect.

trigger_word_detected.description: A trigger word was seen on a blocked page (mitmproxy) or on-screen (Mac accessibility scan).

daemon_unloaded_recovered.description: The macOS daemon had stopped running; the watchdog relaunched it.

watchdog_or_daemon_reregistered.description: The daemon/watchdog needed re-registration with launchd on GUI app launch.

mac_tamper_policy.description: Fleet reports a failing tamper policy on the Mac (app removed / daemon stopped).

mac_silent.description: Dead-man's switch: the Mac stopped checking in with Fleet entirely.

mac_back.description: Dead-man's switch: the Mac is checking in again after a mac_silent event.

monitor_degraded.description: The dead-man's switch itself can't reach Fleet (monitor is blind, not a tamper).

mac_code_tampered.description: The Mac's app binaries were built from an uncommitted, locally-modified source tree.

dns_floor_disabled.description: The DNS floor filter was switched off from System Settings without removing the profile.

dns_floor_reenabled.description: The DNS floor filter was switched back on.

sudo_request_approved.description: An elevated (sudo) command on the Mac was approved (allowlist or AI review).

sudo_request_denied.description: An elevated (sudo) command on the Mac was denied.

sudo_request_ai_reviewed.description: An elevated command went through AI review (approved or denied either way).

passcode_rejected.description: A wrong Guardian passcode was entered on the Mac.

passcode_set.description: A Guardian passcode was set for the first time.

protection_removed.description: A protection-reducing removal/disable action was authorized and applied on the Mac.

kill_switch_activated.description: The Mac's emergency kill switch was triggered: the WHOLE app is disabled, not just filtering (DNS/proxy/pf cleared, scanner and GUI app stopped, both daemons unloaded).

kill_switch_restored.description: The kill switch was undone (`otterlingctl restore`) -- protection and DNS/proxy settings are back to how they were right before it fired.

VPN_BLOCK.description: The phone's content filter VPN blocked a request.

WATCHED_APP.description: A watched app was opened on the phone.

TRIGGER_WORD.description: A trigger word was seen on-screen on the phone (accessibility scan).

UPDATE_REQUESTED.description: An app update was requested from the phone's Settings.

APP_UPDATE.description: An app update finished installing on the phone.

HABIT_UNLOCK.description: Reserved for a future habit-based unlock feature -- not currently triggered anywhere.

ACCESSIBILITY_DISABLED.description: The Accessibility service (focus-guard) was turned off on the phone.

ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE_INTERRUPTED.description: The Accessibility service was interrupted by the OS.

ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE_DESTROYED.description: The Accessibility service process was destroyed.

ADMIN_DISABLE_REQUESTED.description: Removing Device Admin/Device Owner was requested on the phone.

ADMIN_DISABLED.description: Device Admin/Device Owner was actually disabled.

PROTECTION_OFF.description: Overall phone protection was turned off.

ACCOUNTABILITY_ALERTS_DISABLED.description: Accountability-partner alerts were turned off in Settings.

ACCOUNTABILITY_PARTNER_REMOVED.description: An accountability partner's number was removed.

RESTRICTION_DISABLED_BY_USER.description: A device restriction was turned off by the phone's user.

UNINSTALL_PROTECTION_DISABLED_BY_USER.description: Uninstall protection was turned off by the phone's user.

CONTENT_FILTER_DISABLED_BY_USER.description: The phone's content filter VPN was turned off by the user.

APP_UNBLOCKED_BY_USER.description: A blocked app was unblocked by the user.

RESTRICTION_DRIFT.description: A device restriction was found reverted and got re-applied.

CONTENT_FILTER_DRIFT.description: The content filter VPN was found off and got re-enabled.

APP_BLOCK_DRIFT.description: A blocked app was found unblocked and got re-blocked.

NSFW_SCREENSHOT_DETECTED.description: A screenshot uploaded for server-side classification came back NSFW; that app was blocked for 15 minutes.

habit_completed.description: A device reported a global habit done for the day (POST /dashboard-api/habits/<id>/complete) -- shows up in that device's Activity Log so a guardian can spot a suspicious one, especially for a habit not marked requiresProof.

pin_bruteforce_suspected.description: 10 wrong Guardian PIN guesses in a row (POST /dashboard-api/pin/verify) -- possible brute-force attempt against Settings on a phone, not just a mistyped PIN.

guardian_login_bruteforce_suspected.description: 10 wrong dashboard/review login attempts in a row -- possible brute-force attempt against the guardian password.

TEST_REPORT.description: Guardian pressed "Send test report" in Global Settings to verify the alert pipeline (ntfy push + accountability-partner SMS) is wired up.
